eips.title: Frame Transaction
eips.summary: Frame transaction spec freeze for DevNet 0 discussed; SFI'd for Hegota; collaboration with 8130 on unified transaction type ongoing.

moments.context: Marc recapped that 8141 and 8130 proponents are working towards a single transaction type or coexisting types.
Marc noted 8141 was SFI'd on last Thursday's ACDE call to signal native AA is an absolute priority in the Hegota fork.
Lightclient said no spec updates this week but has been chatting with Chris about improving frames for L1/L2 interoperability.
Lightclient proposed freezing the spec for DevNet 0, with new changes going to DevNet 1; multiple client teams reported readiness.
Chris presented ideas for generalizing the verify frame so that both 8130 and 8141 authority models can use the same transaction envelope.
Marc asked Chris if he was ready to make specific proposals back into 8141; Chris said he would continue contributing ideas.
Lightclient said he will schedule DevNet 0 for Frames next week and asked people to keep discussing ideas in the 8141 R&D Discord channel.

eips.title: Keystore Accounts
eips.summary: Keystore Accounts authority model compared with 8141; Chris explored how both could share one verify frame and transaction envelope.

moments.context: Marc noted proponents of 8130 and 8141 are searching for common ground on a native AA transaction type.
Chris described 8130's externally-owned-account authority model using keystore-managed authenticators and how it differs from 8141's code-as-authority.
Chris explained how the verify frame data field differs between 8130 chains (defined authenticator interface, no selector needed) and 8141 chains (wallet selector required).
Chris confirmed 8130 is not a one-way door and can work on L1, and he will keep contributing ideas to 8141.

eips.title: Keyed Nonces for Frame Transactions
eips.summary: Lightclient proposed dropping keyed nonces in favour of a canonical frame; also running on ethrex's Hegota devnet.

moments.context: Lightclient said in chat he would be interested in dropping EIP-8250 in favour of just a canonical frame, like the one used for expiry.
Toni Wahrstätter corrected in chat that lightclient meant 8272 — 8250 is keyed nonces.
Iván posted that ethrex's closed Hegota devnet includes an EIP-8250 implementation.

eips.title: Recent Roots for Frame Transactions
eips.summary: Lightclient proposed moving Recent Roots out of the transaction envelope into a canonical frame as an out-of-protocol mempool rule.

moments.context: Lightclient raised the idea of treating 8272 recent roots as out-of-protocol canonical frames rather than envelope changes, citing maintenance and consensus risk.
Toni Wahrstätter said the initial motivation was gas costs and asked if removing it from the envelope changes gas accounting.
Soispoke raised concerns that moving recent roots out of the envelope would consume verify-frame gas, potentially 40k gas for 16 roots.
Toni suggested exempting recent-root gas from the verify-frame limit since the limit is only for the mempool and the behavior is deterministic.
Soispoke asked whether an EIP would still be warranted; lightclient said yes, as a mempool rule spec rather than a protocol change.
Iván posted that ethrex's closed Hegota devnet includes an EIP-8272 implementation.

eips.title: Code-Controlled EOA Delegation
eips.summary: Discussed as the mechanism to remove the K1 key and rotate to code-only authority; lightclient said he prefers EIP-8298 instead.

moments.context: Chris mentioned 7851 as the proposal to remove the K1 key and specify code-only authority, saying it matters for ensuring no one-way doors in authority models.
Lightclient said in chat he hopes for EIP-8298 instead of 7851, noting the principle is similar.
Chris revisited 7851 in the context of an AA precompile that could handle authority rotation.

eips.title: SETCODEFROM Code Reuse Instruction
eips.summary: Lightclient mentioned preferring 8298 over 7851 for code reuse delegation in the verify step.

moments.context: Lightclient posted a link to EIP-8298 in chat saying he hopes for this instead of 7851.

eips.title: Set Code for EOAs
eips.summary: Referenced as an example of delegation that could be handled via a precompile frame instead of envelope changes.

moments.context: Chris suggested an AA precompile could handle 7702 delegation as a frame call rather than an envelope-level feature.
Derek asked Chris to clarify the AA precompile; Chris confirmed it could serve as a new 7702 delegation path.

eips.title: In-mempool signature and proof aggregation
eips.summary: In-mempool signature and proof aggregation discussed in context of post-quantum needs and relationship to LeanVM and Stark-based compression.

moments.context: Luca asked in chat if the signature frame idea is similar to 8288 and whether it could unify with the STARK frame.
Soispoke said 8288 is needed for post-quantum private transactions; lightclient argued native signature aggregation should not wait for ZK EVM readiness.
Lightclient discussed LeanVM as purpose-built for signature aggregation, distinguishing it from general ZK EVM compute that 8288 might rely on.
